premise: I am an immortal god who got bored and came down to live among mortals as a traveling merchant.

draft.premise: I am an immortal god who got bored and came down to live among mortals as a traveling merchant.

world.title: The Vagrant Divine
world.era: Medieval era: horse-drawn wagons, parchment ledgers, and basic steel weaponry

extraordinary.reach: Gods hold absolute dominion over natural laws, but their power is tethered to their divine domains and celestial status.
Mortals can channel ambient mana to light fires, heal small physical scrapes, or move objects over short distances.

rules.text: Gods do not age and cannot die of mortal sickness or time, remaining forever as they are.
Unveiling a god's true celestial aura causes massive spiritual shockwaves that can blind or overwhelm nearby mortals.
Performing overt miracles or using massive divine magic makes a god's spiritual signature burn brightly, instantly alerting the Celestial Court.

peoples.name: Humans
peoples.description: The mortal populace of the Oster Valley, living simple lives of farming, trading, and craftsmanship.
peoples.culture: A practical and deeply superstitious people who honor local spirits and fear the celestial deities.

peoples.name: Celestial Spirits
peoples.description: Beings of pure divine light who serve the gods as messengers, arbiters, and enforcers of heavenly law.
peoples.culture: A highly ordered society bound by strict heavenly decrees and celestial hierarchy.

nature: The laws of gravity and weather are overseen by minor, slumbering regional spirits who can be nudged by divine presence.

travel.description: Travel is slow, carried out on foot, horseback, or heavy wooden wagons along muddy dirt roads.

medicine.healing: Mortal medicine is limited to simple herbal poultices and basic bandaging. Serious diseases are often fatal without rare magical interventions.

laws.text: All merchants trading within city walls must register with the regional Merchant Guild and pay a monthly silver tax.

norms: Revealing oneself as a god to common mortals is viewed as an act of reckless destruction due to the mental toll it inflicts.

places.name: Oster Valley
places.description: A vast, sweeping valley cradled by jagged mountains, dotted with small farming villages and dense pine forests.

places.name: Village of Kerr
places.description: A quiet farming settlement known for its sweet wheat fields and simple, hardworking mortal inhabitants.

places.name: The High Road
places.description: A winding dirt trade route that cuts through the pine forests of the valley, connecting outlying villages to the grand city of Solitude.

places.name: City of Solitude
places.description: A bustling trading hub walled with white stone, where merchants from across the continent exchange spices, silks, and ores.

places.name: The Golden Scales
places.description: The grand, oak-paneled headquarters of the regional Merchant Guild in Solitude, smelling of ink, wax, and expensive tobacco.

factions.name: The Oster Merchant Guild
factions.description: A wealthy association of mortal traders who regulate all commerce, tariffs, and market spaces in the region.
factions.goal: Maximize regional profits and squeeze out independent, tax-evading travelers.
factions.methods: Deploying guild arbiters to check merchant papers and confiscating unregistered cargo.
factions.strength: High economic leverage, backed by paid municipal guards.
secrets: They systematically bribe the city watch to ignore illegal spice smuggling.

factions.name: The Celestial Court
factions.description: The divine bureaucracy of gods and spirits who govern natural laws and maintain cosmic order from the upper spheres.
factions.goal: Keep all divine beings within their designated celestial domains to prevent disruption of the mortal plane.
factions.methods: Sending spiritual trackers and heralds to search for wayward deities.
factions.strength: Limitless spiritual power and divine authority.
secrets: They fear that a god living permanently as a mortal will permanently weaken the heavenly barrier.

npcs.name: Elara of Oster
npcs.description: A sharp-eyed, practical mortal merchant who travels the high roads selling woven wool and dried medicinal herbs.
npcs.appearance: A young woman in her mid-twenties with wind-burnt cheeks, dark braided hair, wearing a sturdy green woolen cloak and leather riding boots.

wants: To earn enough silver to buy a permanent shopfront in Solitude's main market square.

skills.name: Barter
skills.notes: Excellent at finding the middle ground in haggling.

skills.name: Survival
skills.notes: Knows how to camp and start fires in rainy weather.

npcs.name: Phaeton
npcs.description: A celestial spirit sent disguised as a human scholar to investigate anomalies and search for the missing divinity.
npcs.appearance: An incredibly neat, pale man wearing pristine grey scholars' robes that never seem to collect road dust, carrying a heavy brass-bound ledger.

wants: To quickly find the missing god and return to the peaceful upper realms.

skills.name: Investigation
skills.notes: Superb at spotting subtle magical or divine residue left on ordinary objects.

skills.name: Divine Lore
skills.notes: Has memorized the seals and signatures of almost every major deity.

agenda.goal: Locate the divine signature of the missing god Oros and report it immediately to the Upper Heavens.
agenda.method: Inspect local market ledgers for goods that are too perfect to be mortal-made.
agenda.secret: He has a tracking talisman that vibrates whenever it comes within fifty paces of a disguised deity.

secrets: He secretly despises the field assignment and misses his celestial desk.

clocks.name: The Celestial Court's Search
steps: A quiet murmur spreads through the local temples as high priests feel a distant, missing presence.
Celestial scribe Phaeton arrives in Solitude to inspect local trading records for signs of divine luck.
Minor divine spirits are dispatched to set up spiritual checkpoints on the valley roads.
A high-ranking archon of the Celestial Court descends to personally retrieve the wayward deity.

threads.title: Outrunning the Heavens
threads.stakes: If the Celestial Court locates you, your peaceful holiday as a mortal merchant will be forcibly brought to an end.

mysteries.question: What caused the Celestial Court to target the Oster Valley for their search?
mysteries.answer: A local shrine-keeper in Solitude was sold a bundle of linen that you accidentally infused with a trace of your divine 'hearth' aura, causing the cloth to stay perfectly clean and warm. He reported this minor miracle to the priesthood.
clues: A rumor of a 'miraculous self-warming blanket' circulating among Solitude's high nobility.
The guild registers noting a shipment of common linens sold at ten times their normal price due to mysterious properties.

known_facts: The Celestial Court monitors cosmic balances and dislikes gods leaving their stations.
The name you go by now is Aurelius, and you travel with a simple horse-drawn merchant cart.

positions: sitting comfortably on the bench of your wooden merchant wagon
walking alongside her own horse-drawn cart
props: The worn leather reins in your hands
A heavy wooden chest filled with common spices behind your seat
opening.situation: You are trotting down the dusty High Road toward Solitude, enjoying the simple mortal scent of pine needles, when Elara points toward a distant column of smoke on the horizon.

world.summary: An immortal deity, utterly bored of heavenly splendor, has descended to earth to live as a humble traveling merchant named Aurelius. While enjoying the simple mortal pleasures of the open road, the bureaucracy of the heavens is fast closing in to track down their missing god.

character.name: Aurelius
character.description: A calm, exceptionally poised merchant with an air of ancient wisdom that belies his youthful mortal appearance.
character.appearance: A handsome man in his late twenties with neat brown hair, deep amber eyes, wearing a simple but well-kept gray wool tunic and a dark leather merchant's vest.

skills.name: Appraisal
skills.notes: You can determine the true quality, origin, and history of any mortal item at a single glance.

skills.name: Deception
skills.notes: Crucial for keeping your divine identity perfectly concealed under a simple mortal cover story.

skills.name: Divine Lore
skills.notes: An intimate, personal knowledge of heavenly hierarchy, celestial law, and divine physics.

skills.name: Barter
skills.notes: You've quickly picked up the nuances of mortal trade, though you sometimes find their obsession with copper amusing.

traits.name: Eternally Serene
traits.description: Having witnessed the rise and fall of whole civilizations, you are virtually immune to mortal panic or sudden terror.

powers.name: The Divine Mask
limits: Cannot completely hide your divine aura from specialized tracking talismans when within close proximity.

costs.text: Requires conscious focus to maintain when experiencing extreme physical shock.

powers.name: Minor Miracle
limits: Using this power to alter probability, mend broken matter, or conjure items leaves a faint spiritual signature that celestial trackers can detect.

costs.text: A brief moment of spiritual focus, followed by potential detection if used repeatedly in the same area.

loves: the sound of rain on a canvas wagon cover
fears: returning to boring celestial desk work
wants: To experience the simple, unpredictable ups and downs of a traveling merchant's life.

items.name: Traveler's Wagon
items.description: A sturdy two-wheeled wooden cart with a white canvas cover, pulled by a reliable old draft horse named Barnaby.

items.name: Fine Spices and Silks
items.description: A selection of common trade goods, perfectly sorted and kept in neat wooden crates in the back of your wagon.

items.name: Brass Balance Scales
items.description: A standard merchant's scale for weighing coins, metals, and precious herbs.

character.title: Independent Merchant

connections.name: Elara of Oster
connections.note: A friendly fellow merchant who showed you how to properly grease a wagon wheel when you first started.

backstory: For three thousand years, you sat upon a gilded throne in the high heavens, answering mundane prayers and managing the celestial bureaucracy of horizons.
Thoroughly bored of perfection, you decided to pack a single wooden cart with mortal goods, slip past the celestial gatekeepers, and wander the muddy roads of the mortal plane.
For the past few months, you have thoroughly enjoyed the simple tasks of setting up camp, sharing cheap stew with other travelers, and haggling over a handful of silver.
